beginner.summary: For Python developers, data engineers and AI application builders who have not used Chroma before. Covers installing the chromadb package, the ephemeral, persistent and HTTP clients, collections, adding, querying, getting, updating, upserting and deleting records, metadata filters with where and document filters with where_document, the default all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding function and hosted or local alternatives, precomputed embeddings, the l2, cosine and ip distance spaces, chunking documents, running the Chroma server with chroma run and Docker, the JavaScript/TypeScript client, testing with pytest, and an FAQ search capstone.
prerequisites: Writes and runs Python 3.10+ scripts, creates virtual environments and installs packages with pip or uv
Understands at a conceptual level that an embedding is a list of numbers representing text meaning
Has a laptop with rights to install Python packages and Docker Desktop or Docker Engine, plus about 2 GB of free disk space for models and data
outcomes: Choose between EphemeralClient, PersistentClient and HttpClient and create, list, modify and delete Chroma collections
Load, query, get, update, upsert and delete records with IDs, documents, metadata and embeddings, including where and where_document filters
Select an embedding function and distance space for a collection and explain how each choice affects query distances
Run Chroma as a server with chroma run or Docker with persistent storage and call it from Python and TypeScript clients with tested code

intermediate.summary: For developers who can already build a small Chroma application and now need to run it reliably for a team or product. Covers the Chroma 1.x storage layout, collection configuration and HNSW parameters, recall measurement, batched ingestion, custom and local embedding functions, combined filters, pagination and export, multi-modal collections with OpenCLIP, tenants and databases, server config.yaml settings, the v2 REST API, token checks at a reverse proxy, async clients, LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations, a RAG pipeline, retrieval evaluation and embedding model migration, ending with a multi-tenant document assistant capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the Chroma beginner level or has built an application that adds, queries and filters records in Chroma
Comfortable with Docker, environment variables, HTTP status codes and reading JSON responses with curl
Has access to an embedding provider (an OpenAI API key or a local Ollama install) and an LLM for the RAG exercises
outcomes: Configure HNSW parameters per collection, measure recall@k against brute-force search and tune ef_search for a latency target
Ingest large datasets in batches with custom, local or multi-modal embedding functions and export collections safely
Operate a Chroma server with config.yaml, tenants and databases, the v2 REST API and token checks enforced at a reverse proxy
Build and evaluate LangChain and LlamaIndex RAG pipelines on Chroma and migrate collections to a new embedding model without downtime

advanced.summary: For engineers who run Chroma in production or design search systems on it. Covers Chroma Cloud onboarding with the Chroma CLI and CloudClient, the Cloud Search API with Search, K, Knn, Rrf and GroupBy, collection Schema and index control, sparse vectors and BM25, hybrid ranking, full-text and regex matching, SPANN tuning, collection forking and copying data to the cloud, self-hosting on Kubernetes with Helm, single-node limits and the components of distributed Chroma, backups and disaster recovery, load testing, memory sizing, OpenTelemetry tracing, hardening and version upgrades, finishing with a production hybrid search platform capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the Chroma intermediate level or has operated a Chroma server with batched ingestion, filters and retrieval evaluation
Works confidently with Kubernetes (kubectl, Helm, PersistentVolumeClaims) and Linux storage and networking
Has a Chroma Cloud account or can create one, plus a Kubernetes cluster such as kind, minikube or a managed cluster
outcomes: Build dense, sparse and hybrid searches with the Chroma Cloud Search API and Schema, and tune ranking with Rrf weights and GroupBy
Choose between self-hosted single-node Chroma, distributed Chroma and Chroma Cloud based on measured load, memory and availability needs
Deploy Chroma on Kubernetes with persistence, tracing, network controls and a tested backup and restore procedure
Plan and execute version upgrades and data moves between local Chroma and Chroma Cloud with verified counts and quality
